steps.text: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and stir in the ground beef, onion, green and red peppers, beef bullion, salt, seasoned salt, and pepper. Cook and stir until the beef is crumbly, evenly browned, and no longer pink. Drain and discard any excess grease. Stir in the water and rice. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until the rice is tender, and the liquid has been absorbed, 20 to 25 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Ann's Dirty Rice
raw_recipe.description: A quick and colorful one-pot meal with bits of onion, green, and red bell peppers cooked with ground beef and rice.
raw_recipe.name: Ann's Dirty Rice

review.reviewBody: This is a good base recipe, easy to work with and make the way you want. I added a can of red beans, some garlic powder, Adobo seasoning and a couple of dashes of cayenne. I also used brown rice instead of white. Very easy and inexpensive! Thanks for sharing.

Very yummy. I used brown rice instead of white and had to add three cups of water instead of one. I cooked the rice for 10 min before adding to the meat. Then mixed with ground turkey and cooked for 30-35 min until rice was tender. I also used 1 beef cube per each cup of water added. Substituted ground turkey for beef and added one chopped chicken/bell pepper sausage link from Costco and a half cup of powdered parmesan to the ground turkey. My two year old daughter and family loved it!

Good start but missing a lot. I add ½ pound of andouille Cajun sausage, 2 stalks of celery, a few dashes for Louisiana Hot Sauce, 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce 1 teaspoon of dried parsley. I also saute the rice a little bit with the vegetables, before I add the liquid, to brown it a slight bit. A bay leaf is a nice addition and some thyme too, but not a must have, just adds lots of good flavor.
Quick and easy. I added 3 stalks of celery (chopped), 1/2 tsp garlic powder, and 1/2 cup of more water after simmering so the rice doesn’t dry out.

Good start but missing a lot. I add ½ pound of andouille Cajun sausage, 2 stalks of celery, a few dashes for Louisiana Hot Sauce, 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce 1 teaspoon of dried parsley. I also saute the rice a little bit with the vegetables, before I add the liquid, to brown it a slight bit. A bay leaf is a nice addition and some thyme too, but not a must have, just adds lots of good flavor.

Sooo good. Followed basic recipe idea. Also used condensed French onion soup (instead of bullion), a tablespoon or two of pickle juice, a little water and a glob of salsa for the liquid. Added diced carrots, frozen corn and frozen green beans. Used mixed rice instead of plain white. Skipped salts. Wow. Simple and delicious!

I took her concept and twisted it a bit, I added orange, yellow, and red peppers, Italian hot sausage along with the ground beef, jalapeno peppers, and mushrooms. I stir fried the rice mix all together with soy sauce and topped with scallions. But it came out amazing. My kids raced to the stove for seconds as did I...lol

Made it twice. First time with ground beef- added canned diced tomatoes with garlic. Awesome. Round 2-skipped the ground beef, added a package of Aidells andouille sausage, diced and some garlic and olive oil. Either way, my very sophisticated husband was in heaven. Comfort food at its best. Don’t skip the seasoned salt or the beef bouillon. (I used sodium free bouillon and it worked fine- just needed a little extra salt)

It is a good base, but the flavor is really bland, despite all the wonderful veggies. My son wanted to get creative, and add A1 sauce, and it actually was a really good addition. We took about a tablespoon of A1 and mixed it with about 1/4 c of water to dilute and make dispersion easier and mixed it in with the completed dish and stirred it in over low heat. Next time, I may just add it with the water before cooking the rice. Or, using a more flavorful meat, such as sausage would make it even better!

This was delicious and makes A LOT.
I added minced gizzards that I had booked for an hour, and cooked the rice in that stock.
Good recipe. I use ground turkey and andouille sausage. I also use beef seasoning because I didn’t have any beef granules . I also use pre chopped peppers. I added in some cajun seasoning.

My husband and I loved this recipe. He loved it enough to want it for dinner the next night, and believe me, this rarely happens! He asked me if I would make it for dinner again this week but I don't have all the ingredients, so he volunteered to go get what I needed.....another shocking thing happening!! He hates grocery shopping. Thanks for posting this recipe that is now a regular here. Ann Payne
Loved it!!!!

This was so good!.......The only thing we did different was we used 3 cups water and 3 beef bouillon cubes. I only had one red pepper so we only used 1 pepper. Sprinkled some paprika and pepper in it. We will be having this one again.
This isn't it. Not enough Cajun flavor and Dirty rice needs ground pork. Promising start but it needs work.
Absolutely delicious!!! My granddaughter loves it and so do I and my neighbours. It is on my bi-weekly dinner rotation and I can't see it going anywhere else in the near future.
ABSOLUTELY DELISH! I added a little cumin and cilantro. Can't wait to make it again!

I was stuck at the house and was hungry. I had a half pound of ground beef I needed to do something with, plus a red bell pepper and onions. Out of the blue I thought of dirty rice. I found this recipe and had everything at hand I needed. I cooked up the ground beef and added an extra teaspoon of beef bouillon power since I was short on the ground beef. It tastes wonderful. Even with half the ground beef, it still feels like there is plenty in the dish. This was easy to make. Definitely a keeper! Thanks for sharing.

This is a family favorite. Made as is it’s great. It’s also a great base recipe if you want to add some heat, or corn, I’ve even added some little necks in the shells at the end. This is a family staple in our home.

My little boys (8 & 12) LOVE this dish. It's so simple to prepare. I make it every 4-6 weeks as part of the meal rotation and they're always so happy. Today I'll be sharing with my elderly uncle since I know it's good and he doesn't like to cook. Highly recommend this recipe!
